cited.quote: NABARD has sanctioned a three year project (2017-18 to 2019-20), for an outlay of Rs.22.65 crore

rationale: C1 reports a NABARD-sanctioned project (from 2017-18) building water harvesting structures in Chittar sub-basin, and reclamation of saline problem soils (Cuddalore, Ramanathapuram, Tirunelveli). These cover parts of water systems and land reclamation, but only in a few districts, and no GO date is given. C2 is a 2012 wasteland scheme with no allotment. Partial; date is year-level only.

cited.quote: Administrative approval and financial sanction for Implementation of Tamil Nadu Cotton Cultivation Mission

rationale: C4 is a GO (2020-07-22) sanctioning the Cotton Cultivation Mission to increase cotton production, but its target is raising area to 6 lakh acres from about 4 lakh and ELS area to 30,000 Ha, far below a twofold production increase (C5, C1). The mission pre-dates the government (2014-15). So an order exists, with materially reduced scope.

cited.quote: Administrative approval and financial sanction for Implementation of Tamil Nadu Cotton Cultivation Mission

rationale: C5 is the GO of 2020-07-22 sanctioning the Tamil Nadu Cotton Cultivation Mission with a focus on Integrated Pest Management over 10,000 Ha. This is a departmental cotton production drive, but a continuation of a 2014-15 mission and not aimed at doubling output (target 6 lakh acres, ELS 30,000 Ha). Materially reduced scope relative to doubling.

cited.quote: hereby accord administrative approval for implementation of the project

rationale: C2 is G.O.(D) No.43 dated 01.11.2019 according administrative approval and financial sanction of Rs.9,98,57,382 to ELCOT for enhancement of Cloud Infrastructure and extension of DR facility. This is a dedicated official step for enhancing cloud operations. C1 (2017) describes the earlier cloud set-up and is not a dated order.

cited.quote: Accordingly, from 24.05.2016 onwards, the TASMAC retail vending liquor shops and the bars attached thereto

rationale: C2 (policy note 2018-19) states the government's phased policy: as a first step, TASMAC working hours were reduced from 24.05.2016 and 1000 shops closed in 2016-17. Policy note exists and phased steps were taken, but total prohibition is not achieved and no GO is quoted. Partial; date is the effective date written in C2.

cited.quote: Amendment to the Tamil Nadu Liquor (Supply by Wholesale) Rules, 1983

rationale: C4 and C5 (GO 28 of 2019) amend Rule 22 only to carry the FSSAI statutory health warning; it is not an enforcement of prohibition. C1-C3 describe existing enforcement and the existing Preventive Detention Act (1982). No extract shows a new legislation or amendment to enforce prohibition.

cited.quote: free hot cooked nutritious meal is being provided to children in Government Schools, Government aided

rationale: C1-C3 describe the existing Nutritious Meal Programme (hot cooked meals with eggs and variety menus since 2014) for primary children, but none shows breakfast being introduced. C4 and C5 are about marriage assistance and Anganwadi mats. No official step for a breakfast component.

cited.quote: accord administrative sanction for the construction of Groynes at Alanthalai Village in Thiruchendur Taluk
Construction of Groyne at Poothurai in Vilavancode Taluk of Kanniyakumari District at an estimated cost of Rs.14.69 crore

rationale: C2 (G.O.(Ms) No.146, 2020-06-02) accords administrative sanction of Rs.52.46 crore for 7 groynes at Alanthalai, a village subject to sea erosion. C5 reports groyne works built or in progress in Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari and Thiruvallur districts. This is action to construct groynes at erosion-prone places; earlier GOs are not dated in the extracts.

cited.quote: The Government has enhanced the monthly food charges of school hostel boarders from Rs.755 to Rs.900
college hostel boarders from Rs.875 to Rs.1,000 with effect from 1.6.2017

rationale: C2 states the monthly hostel food charges were raised from Rs.755 to Rs.900 (school) and Rs.875 to Rs.1,000 (college) with effect from 1.6.2017, after the government took office. That is a dedicated enhancement measure for the directional promise. C1 shows the revised rates in use; C4 shows the earlier 2013 rates.

cited.quote: From the year 2018-19 the beneficiaries who are undertaking this Pilgrimage has been enhanced from 500 to 600
The scheme of providing financial assistance for Jerusalem Pilgrimage by all sects of Christians

rationale: C1 and C3 show the Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance (Rs.20,000 each) continued every year, with funds released 2016-17 to 2017-18 and enlarged from 500 to 600 pilgrims by G.O. (MS) No.50 dated 31.8.18 (C3). The scheme continued and was expanded. Date is the first dated GO in the extracts; yearly release before that is undated.

cited.quote: idly steamers, library books and electric insect destroyer are supplied to both school and college hostels
Idly cooker-cum-steam boilers and washing machines will be provided to all the hostels in the

rationale: C1 (2017) says idly cooker-cum-steam boilers will be provided to all hostels; C4 (2018) and C2/C3 later say idly steamers are supplied to both school and college hostels of the BC/MBC department and steam boilers to college hostels. Supply is reported, but no GO or exact date is given, so the date is year-level only.

The promise only says to expand an unnamed scheme, so no extract can be matched to it as the same action for the same object. The extracts concern horticulture, supply chain, house building advance and similar unrelated schemes.

cited.quote: The Joint Venture companies, to be eligible for assistance under this scheme, should have minimum 11 % stake of SIDCO

rationale: C4 is G.O.(Ms) No.32 of 09.09.2016 issuing guidelines for the Integrated MSME Growth Park scheme, with private joint-venture companies holding a minimum 11 % SIDCO stake. This is a SIDCO-associated private estate scheme, but the stake (minimum 11 %) differs from the promised up to 10 percent capital, and the capital support details are not shown.

cited.quote: orders were issued for the establishment of new Government Medical College and Hospital at Tiruppur District
orders have been issued for starting of the new Medical College at Namakkal District

rationale: C1 records that the first GO (No.469 dated 15.10.2019) ordered a new Government Medical College at Tiruppur; C5 reports an order for a new medical college at Namakkal, and C2-C4 cover Krishnagiri, Nilgiris and Dindigul. These are administrative orders establishing new colleges, though only medical colleges are shown.

accord Administrative and Financial sanction for a sum of Rs.10,00,00,000/- (Rupees Ten crores only)

rationale: C5 is G.O.(Ms) No.151 dated 26.07.2019, a sanction of funds to upgrade infrastructure in Government Engineering Colleges. C1 (2020-11-27) sanctions Rs.10 crore for classroom complex and compound wall at the Government College of Technology, Coimbatore. Both allocate funds for college infrastructure; C5 is earliest.

rationale: C1 is G.O. Ms No.292 dated 04.08.2020 sanctioning Rs.103.5 crore to procure 500 ambulances to strengthen the 108 emergency service, replacing condemned vehicles and increasing fleet strength (C3). It is an order upgrading 108 operations. C4 and C5 describe apps and GPS but with no dated order.

cited.quote: is permitted to procure 400 Basic Life Support (BLS) Ambulances

rationale: C2 (GO 292, 2020-08-04) sanctions procurement of 500 additional ambulances for the 108 service, an official step. No extract shows they were actually procured or added to the fleet; C3 and C5 report about 940-950 ambulances in operation, and C5 only hires 50 extra ambulances temporarily. Sanctioned but not shown operational.

cited.quote: The initial preparatory works for the setting up of labs are under progress
is establishing a Centre of Excellence and five linked technical Skill Development Institutes

rationale: C1 and C2 say the government is establishing a Centre of Excellence and five linked t-SDIs with Siemens under PPP for students of engineering colleges, polytechnics and ITIs, with preparatory lab works under progress. This is an official step but not yet shown operational. C5 covers internships and C4 a textile policy, not centres.

No extract is about gas pipelines or restricting them from agricultural lands. C1 and C3 describe permission to lay pipelines and optical fibre cables in Government lands (with track rent exempt for agricultural water pipes), which is a different subject. Other extracts concern land ceiling, rice fallow and dryland schemes.
